Independent finite replay in the review: for each positive j≤2^k use the odd part of j modulo four, count exact overlapping substring keys at all legal starts by length until the first singleton, and count P8 windows at lengths 7 (split by start parity) and 16 (bucket by multiplicity). Reported bases: (5;43,47), (9;87,95), (17;175,191).
correctness.rationale: The proof uses zero-based starts, overlapping windows, and a one-ended finite prefix. For same-parity coverage of length sixteen, at most one letter per window has index divisible by 16; the others depend only on index mod 32. The seven representatives at each residue fit in P8 and realize both values of the exceptional letter (alternation on odd arguments, or two odd arguments two apart after division by 2). The independent finite replay matched the disjoint 12/16 parity sets of length seven, the length-sixteen multiplicities (3:16,4:47,5:1), and the three base pairs of starts at lengths 5,9,17. For longer factors, if the first retained odd-position letter occurs at global position 2j+1, the projected factor starts at j. Its parity fixes all reinserted filler bits. The start is either 2j or 2j+1, both legal on the left; on the right only a final filler after the last retained letter can fail to fit. A shorter projected suffix has at least three occurrences, so losing one preserves nonuniqueness. A lifted suffix ends at an odd position and loses none, maintaining the stronger suffix invariant. At length 2d−1 the even-start factors project to length d−1 and cannot be unique; odd-start factors project to length d with no loss. Iteration gives the claimed length and both starts.
residual_risks: The computation certifies only the bases and fixed-length windows; the unbounded conclusion is from the induction. No arbitrary prefix length, cyclic or generalized paperfolding result follows.

value.rationale: The automatic word and its canonical dyadic prefixes are natural, and the global shortest-unique invariant measures finite-prefix distinguishability not captured by ordinary factor complexity. The result gives both a sharp threshold and a complete location classification for an unbounded family. Its suffix invariant addresses a genuine boundary defect in naive desubstitution and is useful for exact prefix occurrence calculations.
